newsitem.title: LATVIA: BOURSE INDEX TO INCLUDE 12 STOCKS.
newsitem.headline: BOURSE INDEX TO INCLUDE 12 STOCKS.

text.p: The Riga bourse on Wednesday said that its index, launched today, will eventually comprise some 12 to 13 stocks against the current nine as more privatised companies, including big utilities join the stock exchange.
The bourse officially launched its market-capitalisation weighted index, tracking nine large cap, active stocks.
"I think the number of companies in the index will grow to reach 12 or 13 by the year end," bourse president Uldis Cerps told a news conference.
Cerps said it was important to have the index in place ahead of the start of trade in big infrastructure companies, expected later this year.
The utilities expected on the bourse include Latvenergo, the monopoly electricity provider, Latvian Gas and oil terminal company Ventspils Nafta.

"It is important to have the index in place when the market enjoys a faster development at the end of summer and autumn," Cerps said. "It will allow porfolio investors to calculate their net assets and performance relative to the index."
The index is aimed at covering 80 percent of the market capitalisation, showing the average price level.
"Given that it is a capitalisation weighted index, price changes will influence it proportionally to the stock size," Cerps said.
The index composition will be updated at least once a quarter and more often if market activity demands it.
